clue.text: Prop stifles short curse in sporting event

indicators.note: to stifle something is to smother it, so the prop wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a brace is a support or prop

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter of the curse goes

parts.note: an oath is a swear word or curse

explanation.surface: A support muffling a clipped expletive during a sports match.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing race on the Thames; 'short' drops the curse's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford and Cambridge rowing contest is a famous example of a sporting fixture.

clue.text: Rough way to stop boxer's first encounter

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the boxer

parts.note: a road is a way
a brush is a brief encounter, as in a brush with the law

explanation.surface: A crude method of stopping a fighter's opening attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way to stop boxer's first' gives B then ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad-brush approach is general and lacking detail, so rough or approximate.

clue.text: Champion needing speed not power

indicators.note: not says the power letter is excluded from the speed

parts.note: pace means speed
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A sports star who needs speed rather than strength.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is an expert or star performer, a champion in their field.

clue.text: Setback upsets comparatively poor bridge opponents

indicators.note: upsets in a down clue turns the word upside down, so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: paler means poorer in comparison, as in a pale imitation
in bridge, South and East sit opposite each other's partnerships, so S and E are opponents

explanation.surface: A defeat that upsets weaker opponents at the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' reverses PALER to RELAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a deterioration after improvement, a setback, especially in health.

clue.text: Be cool and chat about old times as sentimentally appealing

indicators.note: about means moved around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A suggestion to relax and reminisce, described as nostalgic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but rearranges the first two words' letters; 'times' is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate-box pictures are pretty, idealised and twee, so sentimentally attractive.

clue.text: Absent-minded son of a queen?

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, so belonging to one is cat-like, which is catty

explanation.surface: A royal prince described as forgetful, with the question mark hinting at an unroyal queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen here is not royalty but a female cat; 'catty' is read literally as 'cat-like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatty is an informal British word for scatterbrained, forgetful or disorganised.

clue.text: Nobel, say, in key film about explosive

indicators.note: about puts the key and film around the explosive

parts.note: C is a musical key
a mist is a thin film, as on glass
HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: Alfred Nobel appearing in a key film about explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nobel, say' looks like a prize; it is the man, Alfred Nobel, inventor of dynamite.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel was a Swedish scientist of chemistry, an example of the profession.

clue.text: Chap one can't recall hating a bomb going off

indicators.note: going off, like a bomb exploding, scatters these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A forgotten man who hates a bomb that is detonating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' suits the bomb but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A thingamabob is a placeholder name for a person or thing whose name escapes you.

clue.text: Put a song over about women's craft

indicators.note: about says the reversed song surrounds the women's letter
put over together say the song is turned round
over, with put, says the word is reversed

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad
W is the standard abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Someone putting a song across about women's handicraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put ... over' reverses LAY to YAL, which goes round W. 'craft' looks like handiwork but is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawl is a two-masted sailing boat, a kind of craft or vessel.

clue.text: On air making excuse

parts.note: on and over are interchangeable in 'a row on/over money', meaning concerning
an air is a manner or appearance, as is a look

explanation.surface: Something said on the radio being used as a justification.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse a fault is to pardon it, or let it pass unremarked, which is to ignore it.

clue.text: Criticism of clergyman that is ending for now

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a clergyman
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

indicators.note: ending for points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone criticising a vicar, whose career is apparently over for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text inserted a stray 'a,'; the printed page has none.
explanation.definitionFit: A review is a critical assessment of a book, play or film, a piece of criticism.

clue.text: Very popular words describing the man over part of army

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the earlier part above the later

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the words surround the man

parts.note: a text is a body of words
he is the pronoun for the man
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Popular words describing a man who has moved over to a branch of the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense, drawing round. REME is a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: In the extreme is an intensifier meaning to the highest degree, so exceedingly.

clue.text: Poor ground aiding topspin

indicators.note: ground is the past tense of grind, so the letters are crushed and remade

explanation.surface: A tennis remark: an uneven surface helps the player hitting topspin, which is bad news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a court surface; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disappointing falls short of hopes, so it is poor or substandard.

clue.text: Hunt over a year round incomplete set of papers to find owners of land

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the hunt above the year
round says the hunt surrounds the shortened papers

parts.note: to search is to hunt

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter is missing

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A year-long search for missing documents to identify landowners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' drops the last letter of the set of papers; 'over' in a down clue puts the year below.
explanation.definitionFit: The squirearchy is the class of squires, the landed gentry collectively.

clue.text: Western idol with accent that's all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Western film star whose accent wanders all over the map.
explanation.definitionFit: Occidental means of the West, the opposite of oriental.

clue.text: Come to one river after another

indicators.note: after places the first river behind the second in the answer

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river
the Ouse is a river in England (there are several of the name)

explanation.surface: A traveller reaching one river after another along the route.
explanation.walkthrough: The OUSE is an English river; 'another' river is just R.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse is to wake up, which is to come to or regain consciousness.

clue.text: Charity I got out of him originally without regularity

indicators.note: originally here means in an original or novel way, so the letters are arranged afresh
got out of says the letter I is extracted from the word him

explanation.walkthrough: 'I got out of him' leaves HM; CHARITY plus HM are then rearranged, signalled by 'originally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrhythmic, without rhythm, describes something irregular in its beat or pattern.

clue.text: Member in charge seeing what's on the cards?

indicators.note: in puts the limb inside the attack

parts.note: a sortie is an attack or charge by troops
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.definitionFit: Sortilege is divination by drawing lots, a way of foretelling the future.

clue.text: Vague idea of joining Liberal dropped

indicators.note: dropped in a down clue means the Liberal letter moves lower in the word

parts.note: linking means joining

explanation.surface: A vague notion of joining the Liberals, since dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' moves the L of LINKING further down the column.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight suspicion or hint, a vague notion.

clue.text: I shoot back, going round a capital and port

indicators.note: going round means the reversed letters encircle the single letter
back says the pair of words is read from right to left

parts.note: a bud is a young shoot on a plant

explanation.surface: A gunman firing back while circling a city by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns I BUD into DUBI, which goes round A. The OCR text added a stray '19' and 'itas'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is both the chief city of its emirate and a major Gulf seaport.

clue.text: Gathering up rarely unfinished rough sketches

explanation.definitionFit: Doodles are aimless scribbles, rough drawings made idly.

clue.text: Demand effort and expose oneself to difficulties

the idiom for inviting problems by reckless behaviour

clue.text: Chap swindling celebrities from the south

explanation.walkthrough: A spiv is British slang for a flashy petty swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiv is a small-time crook dealing in shady goods, a man who swindles.

clue.text: Money for jam, cream and the jug picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the words are judged by sound

explanation.surface: A list of picnic items: cash for jam, cream and the milk jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money for jam' is a British idiom for something easily done; a picnic means the same ('no picnic').
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal terms for an easy task that requires little effort.

clue.text: Torch found by soldiers miles away in hole

parts.note: men is a common word for soldiers, the ranks

clue.text: A short man fighting knight

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier, a fighting man

explanation.walkthrough: 'A short' looks like a small man; a short is a small measure of spirits, as served in a British pub.

clue.text: Nothing gained by hollow victory, say, after set-back on a tour

indicators.note: after puts the turned example word behind the a
gained by says the empty victory takes in the zero letter
hollow means emptied of its middle, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what 'say' means

clue.text: Individual ringing about crime initially ignored

indicators.note: about means surrounding the other piece

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells
